title: a house built on five
hook: not a checklist: a building, and the building is made of time
carry: five things that hold a life up

segments.voice: Yesterday: salaam. Your line was peace, upon you. Today, the whole shape of a Muslim life, in one sitting. Day nine.

The five pillars of Islam often get learned like a list for a test. Witness. Prayer. Giving. Fasting. Pilgrimage. Five boxes, done. Said that way, it sounds like a checklist. But the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ didn't describe them as a list. He described them as a building. And the building turns out to be made of time.
screen: `FIVE WORDS, FIVE BOXES?` → `NOT A CHECKLIST.` → `A BUILDING.`

segments.voice: Islam is built on five, a saying of the Prophet goes. Built, like a house; pillars are what keep the roof up. One: the shahada, the witness. There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God. One sentence, said to become Muslim and said inside every prayer. Its clock is always. Two: salat, prayer, five times a day, at times that move with the sun. Its clock is the day. Three: zakat, giving a set share of savings to people in need, once a year. Four: sawm, the Ramadan fast you met on day six. Their clock is the year. Five: hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, once in a lifetime. Its clock is a life. Now look at the shape. Always. Every day. Every year. Once in a life. Circles inside circles. And the house fits the person living in it: the Qur'an lets the sick and the traveler make up missed fast days, and asks for the hajj only from those able to make the journey. Muslims also draw the house in more than one way. Sunni teaching usually names these five as the pillars. Shia teaching usually speaks of roots, the core beliefs, and branches, the practices: the witness lives in the roots, and prayer, fasting, giving and pilgrimage among the branches. Same house, drawn two ways.
screen: `ISLAM IS BUILT ON FIVE.` · `ALWAYS, DAILY, YEARLY, ONCE.` · `BUILT TO FIT THE PERSON.` · `ROOTS AND BRANCHES: DRAWN TWO WAYS.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably. The pillars are circles of time, so borrow the shape. Bring to mind something that holds up your day, and let it stay a moment. Then something that holds up your year. Then something you'd want to do once in your life. Nothing to do about any of them. Just see what's holding you up.
The five pillars. Witness, prayer, giving, fasting, pilgrimage: not five boxes but a house built on five. Ninth word.
Your line: five things that hold a life up. Always, daily, yearly, once. Day nine.

howItsDone: Muslims keep the five together: the shahada as the core of faith, the five daily prayers, zakat given yearly, the Ramadan fast, and the hajj once in a lifetime for those able. Shia Muslims keep the same practices and describe the faith as roots (beliefs) and branches (practices).

original.note: Arabic: "the pillars of Islam." arkan is the plural of rukn, a pillar or supporting corner.

trapdoor: what you thought: five rules to tick off.
what it means: five practices a life is built on — "Islam is built on five," in a hadith in Bukhari and Muslim.
what a scholar hears: the five run on nested clocks: always (shahada), daily (salat), yearly (zakat, sawm), once in a life (hajj). Shia teaching draws the same house as roots and branches.
